subject: MAP sprint: priority lanes & staged signature approach for MSA / DPA / Order Form
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP kickoff + procurement constraints (Greenfield Health)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the hosting options. Procurement and security have started their parallel reviews and asked for a concrete mutual action plan (MAP) so they can map approvals to their sprint windows. A few constraints up front:

- Procurement has a monthly board purchasing window on the 20th of each month.
- Security requires SOC evidence + a short PII flow diagram before signing the DPA.
- Legal prefers to sequence the Order Form (commercial terms) and MSA signing to align with internal budget beats; they may request redlines to the indemnity clause.

I've attached our standard security questionnaire (GFH_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf). Could you send a MAP with milestone dates and call out which artifacts must be complete for each procurement window?

Given our timeline, procurement would like a staged signature option (e.g., limited-scope order form or PO to start pilot, MSA to follow, full DPA after security sign-off). Is this something Redwood can support?

Appreciate a concise plan — procurement prefers a one-page milestone table.

Best,
Samantha Lee
VP, Digital Programs
Greenfield Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-09T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + procurement constraints (Greenfield Health)

Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Quick reply with a proposed MAP sprint and a staged-signature option; attaching the draft MAP workbook (MAP-draft-Redwood-Greenfield.xlsx). High-level proposal below (we'll format as a one-pager for procurement):

Proposed priority lanes (brief):
1) Eval / Pilot lane (technical): kickoff -> pilot -> success criteria -> pilot sign-off (2–4 weeks)
2) Security lane: questionnaire review -> SOC + diagram -> security sign-off (3–6 weeks, parallel)
3) Legal lane: redlines -> MSA negotiation -> MSA sign-off (2–4 weeks, can run overlapping with security)
4) Commercial lane: Order Form / PO issuance -> limited-scope order form to enable pilot -> full order form on final sign-off

Staged signature approach (option we can support):
- Stage A (Pilot PO / limited Order Form): greenfield issues PO or signs a limited Order Form to enable a non-production pilot. Minimal risk: capped spend and limited data scope.
- Stage B (MSA): sign MSA (core commercial/legal terms) once legal redlines are agreed — can include a commitment to finalize DPA within X days.
- Stage C (DPA): execute DPA after security completes review (SOC evidence + flow diagram). We can accept a 30–45 day DPA target with a documented mitigation plan for pilot data handling (e.g., pseudonymization, logging restrictions).

Dependencies and gating:
- DPA execution gated on security artifacts.
- Order Form can be issued earlier but must reference the staged-scope and include an escape hatch (ability to terminate pilot without legacy obligations).

Next steps: I'll route the attached MAP draft to our legal lead (karthik) and ask Marissa to co-own commercial timing. Can you confirm procurement windows (is the 20th fixed) and any required PO template language?

I'll convert the above to a one-page for procurement once we have those details.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenfieldhealth.com
Date: 2026-05-10T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + procurement constraints (Greenfield Health)

Thanks Lauren — that structure looks workable. A couple clarifications from procurement/security: 

- The 20th monthly board purchasing window is fixed; if we want to push a minimal pilot PO through for the June window, we need final Order Form language by June 10th.
- The security team needs a short one-pager illustrating data flow and on-hosting controls we will apply during the pilot (pseudonymization + KV cache policies). Can Redwood produce that?
- Legal will ask for an audit logging commitment and a statement that Redwood will not use customer content for model training — are those standard?

Procurement is open to Stage A PO but wants an explicit termination clause and a limited liability cap tied to pilot spend. If you can map which items are mandatory for the June 10th deliverable vs. what can sit in the Stage B/C artifacts, that will help us prioritize.

Happy to jump on a quick 30-min alignment call tomorrow if helpful.

Regards,
Samantha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@greenfieldhealth.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + procurement constraints (Greenfield Health)

Samantha / Lauren — looping in Legal + Commercial notes. We can support a staged-signature flow. Key sequencing and recommended gating (short checklist):

1) Stage A: Limited Order Form / PO to start pilot (target: June 20 purchase window / deliver final Order Form language by June 10)
   - Required for Stage A: Statement of work (scope + duration), capped spend, termination for convenience for pilot, limited liability cap tied to pilot spend, reference to future MSA/DPA ("subject to execution of MSA/DPA").
2) Stage B: MSA execution (target: within 30 days of Stage A)
   - Required for Stage B: Core terms (indemnity, IP, service levels), audit logging commitment, explicit non-use clause for training on customer content. We can accept a commitment to finalize the DPA after MSA is in place.
3) Stage C: DPA execution (target: within 45 days of Stage A)
   - Required for Stage C: SOC evidence (or attestation date), data flow diagram, specific processing terms, subprocessors list.

Risk mitigations we propose:
- Pilot data segregation and pseudonymization controls for Stage A (we will provide a one-pager).
- Limited escalation path and interim SLA for pilot (48–72 hour critical issue response).
- Escrow / recovery process language if required by procurement (we can discuss narrow wording).

Next steps: Marissa will own commercial calendar alignment; Lauren will deliver the one-page security/data flow for the pilot; I'll prepare a short Stage A Order Form template and the staged-signature checklist and share in this thread (attaching Staged-Signature-Checklist.pdf).

If that aligns, request: Samantha, confirm the June 10 deadline and any PO template wording procurement requires so we can prioritize deliverables.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
